newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine appoints new navy commander.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine appoints new navy commander.

text.p: Ukraine on Monday appointed a new navy chief to command the few dozen ships it inherited from the Soviet Union's Black Sea Fleet, over which it has been rowing with Russia since 1991.
Ukrainian television said the new navy chief, Mikhailo Yezhel, 44, had also been appointed deputy defence minister under a decree signed by President Leonid Kuchma.
Ukraine and Russia have long been at odds over how to divide the Black Sea fleet, where to put it and how it should be funded since the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991.

The removal of Yezhel's predecessor Volodymyr Bezkorovainy last week was interpreted as an olive branch to Moscow on the eve of talks in Moscow last week between Kuchma and President Boris Yeltsin which the latter.
But Defence Minister Olexander Kuzmuk was quoted by Ukraine's UNIAN news agency as saying Bezkorovainy and two other top navy officials had not been sacked for political reasons.
Yeltsin said after Kuchma's visit that the two sides had agreed how to divide the fleet, but the Ukrainian leader took a more cautious approach.

Yeltsin also said he planned to make Ukraine his first port of call after an operation on his heart which is expected next month. He said he hoped to sign a much-delayed friendship treaty with Ukraine.
Yezhel, 44, served in the Pacific Fleet until joining Ukraine's fleet in 1993, Ukrainian television said.
